title: Cheese Ravioli with Kale and Sunflower Seed Pesto
changes_from_base: Raw kale, basil, toasted sunflower seeds, chilli flakes and parmesan make a nut-free pesto that replaces the butter sauce, with shop-bought cheese ravioli in place of homemade.
summary: Cheese ravioli tossed in a vivid green pesto of kale, basil and toasted sunflower seeds with a gentle chilli warmth.

ingredients.item: fine sea salt or table salt
fine sea salt or table salt, for the cooking water

steps.title: Boil
steps.text: Get around 4000 ml water boiling hard in a large pot.

steps.title: Blanch
steps.text: Drop in 2 unpeeled garlic cloves for 1 min, refresh under cold water, then peel and chop.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Add 680 g cheese ravioli and 1 tbsp salt, cooking to al dente with frequent stirring; set aside 120 ml of the water before draining and tipping the ravioli back in.

steps.title: Blend
steps.text: Blitz the garlic, 45 g kale, 20 g basil, 40 g parmesan, 70 g sunflower seeds and ½ tsp chilli flakes for 20-30 pulses to a fine grind, scraping down as needed.

steps.title: Stream
steps.text: With the motor running, pour 120 ml olive oil in slowly until fully blended.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Season to taste with ¼ tsp salt and ¼ tsp black pepper.

steps.title: Toss
steps.text: Coat the ravioli in about 240 ml of the kale and sunflower pesto, loosening with a tablespoon of cooking water at a time, then put the rest on the table to pass round.

tips: Toasting the sunflower seeds brings out more savoury depth in the pesto.
The pesto itself is nut-free, but check the ravioli label for egg and nuts.
Add the cooking water bit by bit to reach a glossy, coating consistency.
storage: Keep leftover pesto chilled under a film of oil for up to 2 days. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
